transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, looks like we've got about an hour. quick intros?
[00:10] Dr. Anika Rao (Cascadia): hi all, i'm anika, lead on ML, focused on inference quality for our summarization models.
[00:18] Leo Park (Cascadia): leo, platform, i'll handle env + networking questions.
[00:21] Carlos (Redwood): carlos here, i'll do the technical demo and the bench plan.
[00:27] Tom (Cascadia): tom, product, interested in latency thresholds.
[00:30] Sofia (Cascadia): sofia, security, i'll jump in on compliance.
[00:36] Maya: great, agenda — quick Optimize console demo, then dive into INT8 vs FP8 comparisons, show canary/fallback runbook, and leave time for Q&A.
[00:44] Dr. Anika: sounds good. our main success criteria: keep Rouge/f1 degradation under ~1.5% while getting p95 latency under 300ms for 512 token requests.
[00:56] Carlos: understood — we'll show a typical sensitivity sweep and how Optimize recommends profiles and rollout policies.
[01:04] [01:04] Carlos (screen share): okay pulling up the Optimize dashboard — here's the model catalog, we picked open-llama-70b-qa (note: model name may be transcribed). starting with baseline fp16. baseline p95 is ~420ms on your target sku (we simulated with our sandbox runner).
[01:26] Tom: 420ms is rough for our UI flows, yes — goal is sub-300 for user-facing.
[01:30] Carlos: right, so two levers: lower precision quant (INT8 or FP8) and batching/caching. INT8 often gives largest perf wins but has risk of hallucination/quality drop. FP8 tends to hit sweet spot on many models for minimal quality loss + good speedups.
[01:48] Dr. Anika: are those numbers from your public benchmarks? how reproducible are they on our infra?
[01:54] Carlos: good question. Our public perf profile is measured on controlled hardware. in the sandbox we'll run the exact same prompt set and your instance type — that's why we ask for a sample prompt set. For reproducibility, we recommend: same sequence length distribution, same KV cache warmup, and identical batch size.
[02:18] [02:18] Carlos: let me show an Optimize runbook — start with a sensitivity sweep: run 200-500 eval prompts, measure Rouge/f1 and p95 latency for baseline, INT8, FP8. the console can run calibration jobs and produce a heatmap of fidelity vs latency.
[02:40] [02:40] Carlos (screen): here's a synthetic heatmap — x-axis latency, y-axis Rouge drop. see this region where FP8 gives ~25% latency reduction with only 0.6% Rouge drop, and INT8 gives 45% latency with ~2.3% Rouge drop.
[02:58] Dr. Anika: 2.3% is high for our clinical summarization. we'd be more comfortable if INT8 can be limited to very narrow prompt types only.
[03:06] Carlos: exactly — that's where the canary + fallback runbook helps. you can target INT8 to non-clinical workloads, or route low-risk prompts (e.g., general knowledge QA) to INT8. FP8 can be the global default.
[03:20] Maya: and we have automatic rollback rules if quality drift exceeds X on eval set. show that?
[03:25] Carlos: yep — in the rollout policy you can set thresholds: if eval delta > 1% Rouge or user-sentiment drop, rollback. also set traffic percentages — start 5% traffic for canary, monitor for 24 hours, then increase.
[03:37] [03:37] Leo: technical — how does KV cache behave across precision boundaries? if we switch from fp16 warm cache to int8, do we need to flush?
[03:44] Carlos: good catch. switching precision typically requires a cold start for that particular model variant because KV cache formats differ. Optimize supports staged warm-up: we create a small canary population that primes cache on INT8 nodes before routing production traffic. that reduces cold-start penalty.
[04:02] Sofia: on security — where does the data flow for the sandbox? any logs leaving our VPC?
[04:07] Maya: sandbox can be hosted in Redwood Private or Dedicated depending on your needs. for early tests we can spin a private sandbox in your VPC via peered subnet. logs are kept per config; we can disable pull of user data to hosted analytics and provide audit logs only in your KMS environment.
[04:25] Sofia: we need SOC2 + KMS integration doc and encryption at rest details.
[04:29] Maya: yes, will share.
[04:31] [04:31] Carlos (screen): back to the console — here's an example rollout recipe: step 1: FP8 default; step 2: canary INT8 for 5% traffic with targeted route rules; step 3: monitor metrics (p95, Rouge on sample eval, error rate); step 4: if metrics stable for 24h bump to 20%; step 5: gated roll to 100% or rollback. you can attach automatic fallback so requests failing safety/quality thresholds redirect to FP8 or baseline.
[04:58] Dr. Anika: can we attach custom eval sets and automatic offline scoring?
[05:02] Carlos: yes — Optimize lets you upload prompt sets and expected outputs, run batch scoring during rollout. alerts can trigger when delta exceeds thresholds.
[05:10] Tom: what's the overhead of FP8 vs INT8 in cost?
[05:14] Carlos: cost depends on throughput gains. FP8 often gives similar perf to INT8 on newer kernels with slightly higher accuracy, so net cost can be comparable. Our console shows estimated token-cost-per-request for each profile after the sweep.
[05:28] [05:28] Carlos: quick demo of the bench runner — launching three jobs now: baseline fp16, fp8 profile, int8 profile. each uses your sample distribution we uploaded (note: sample set is generic for demo). results take ~5-8 minutes for a 200 sample sweep.
[05:46] [05:46] Maya: while that's running, can we talk about rollout safety for regulated data? Cascadia mentioned clinical PII in prompts — what's our recommended pattern?
[05:54] Carlos: for PHI/PII we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments so PII never leaves your environment. additionally, enable strict mem-scrubbers, strict logging off, and KMS-managed keys for model artifacts. For pilots, if you must use hosted, we can route through a private peering and ensure no user content is retained in hosted analytics.
[06:15] Sofia: and attestation for key handling?
[06:18] Maya: we have HSM/KMS integrations—Sofia we'll share details and an architecture diagram.
[06:24] [06:24] System: bench jobs complete (demo results shown).
[06:27] Carlos (screen): results table — baseline p95 420ms, fp8 p95 290ms (0.7% Rouge drop), int8 p95 240ms (2.1% Rouge drop). p50 improvements similar. model perplexity rose slightly under INT8.
[06:45] Dr. Anika: those numbers align with your heatmap earlier. So FP8 is within our 1.5% threshold, INT8 is not.
[06:51] Carlos: correct. two options: keep FP8 globally and use INT8 only for narrow routes; or use FP8 now and plan an INT8 narrow rollout where you accept higher risk.
[06:59] Tom: what about user-level routing? can we do per-customer or per-tenant precision?
[07:03] Carlos: yes — routing policies support attributes: tenant id, prompt metadata, time of day. you can write policy rules in the console to route certain tenants to Dedicated INT8 nodes.
[07:14] Dr. Anika: automated rollback — how fast? if INT8 causes hallucinations, can we fallback per-request?
[07:20] Carlos: you can configure synchronous fallback: if a post-scoring check fails (e.g., hallucination classifier), we retry that request on FP8 or baseline. this adds latency for the retry but prevents bad outputs reaching users. asynchronous rollbacks remove traffic from INT8 once thresholds hit.
[07:36] [07:36] Leo: about the cold start again — if we route 5% to INT8, initial requests will be slower until cache warms. is there a warmup API?
[07:44] Carlos: yes — Optimize exposes "prime_cache" job that fires synthetic prompts to fill KV on INT8 nodes before routing. we recommend running prime_cache with a representative set for 10-30 minutes before shifting traffic.
[07:58] Sofia: for compliance we'll need logs of fallback events and rollbacks. where are those stored?
[08:04] Maya: audit logs export to your S3 or to Redwood Console with export controls. in Private you can store logs only in your bucket under KMS.
[08:12] [08:12] Carlos: OK last bit — canary sizing guidance: start 5% or 50 qps (whichever smaller) for 24h, measure per-prompt eval delta and user metrics. if stable, increase gradually. we include a recommended script in the runbook.
[08:28] Dr. Anika: timeline — if we give sample prompts by Friday, can you run benchmarks next week?
[08:32] Maya: yes, Carlos will run them and share CSVs.
[08:35] [08:35] Tom: cost question again — if we go Dedicated INT8 nodes, will that lower per-token cost materially?
[08:41] Carlos: Dedicated reduces variability and gives better throughput; quantization lowers compute per-token. combined you should see unit-cost reductions; we'll quantify in the bench report.
[08:51] [08:51] Carlos (closing demo): recap — FP8 recommended default for Cascadia; INT8 only for non-clinical narrow routes with canary and fallback; prime cache before canary; use Private/Dedicated for PHI. we'll run the sandbox benchmark and share results + runbook and pricing.
[09:05] Maya: thanks everyone. next meeting — bench review next Wed, I'll send invite.
[09:12] Dr. Anika: thanks, talk soon.
